title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint: Bone pain.

HPI: Pt is a 60-year-old male presenting for f/u regarding prostate cancer. Pt is currently receiving chemotherapy for the malignancy. He reports increased dull, aching pain in the lumbar spine and left hip over the last 3 weeks. Describes pain as constant, rated 6/10, worse with weight-bearing. Denies any new neurological deficits or saddle anesthesia. Pt states he has been compliant with current regimen but seeks better pain management.

Medication List:
- Chemotherapy agent (current)
- Naproxen 500mg BID
- Lisinopril 10mg QD

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: No fever, chills, or unintended weight loss.
MSK: Positive for lumbar and hip pain. No joint swelling.
Neuro: No numbness or tingling.
GU: Normal urinary flow, no dysuria.

Social History: Retired; lives with wife. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol use.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had diabetes.

Vitals:
BP: 132/84
HR: 78 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on RA
Weight: 195 lbs

Recent Labs:
Hb: 13.2 g/dL
WBC: 7.4 x 10^9/L
Plt: 210 x 10^9/L
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
eGFR: 82 mL/min/1.73m2

Exam:
Gen: Well-appearing male in no acute distress.
CV: RRR, CTAB.
Resp: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
MSK: Tenderness noted over L4-L5 and left greater trochanteric process. No erythema or warmth.
Neuro: Strength 5/5 throughout. Sensation intact.

Assessment:
1. Prostate cancer, currently receiving chemotherapy.
2. Bone metastases.

Plan:
1. Continue current chemotherapy protocol as scheduled.
2. Address bone metastasis pain: Start low-dose oxycodone 5mg TID PRN for breakthrough pain.
3. Continue current blood pressure medications.
4. Follow up in 4 weeks for symptom review and lab work.

Electronically signed, R. Mensah, DO, 10/14/2026
explanations: Cancer of the prostate under current treatment is a current malignancy: C61.
Bone metastases: C79.51, secondary malignant neoplasm of bone (HCC 18, which outranks the primary-site HCC).

distractors.why: Treatment is still directed at the cancer, so it is current, not history.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in bone, not the liver.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Bone/Other and Unspecified Metastatic Cancer; Acute Leukemia Except Myeloid
